info.desc: Biophilia is the seventh studio album by the Icelandic singer Björk. It was released on October 10, 2011, by One Little Indian Records and distributed by Nonesuch Records in North America and by Universal Music Group in the rest of the world. Björk composed it as a concept album during the 2008–2011 Icelandic financial crisis, exploring the links between nature, music and technology. Billed as the first "app album", Biophilia is a multimedia project released alongside a series of apps linking the album's themes to musicology concepts. It was followed by a series of educational workshops in four continents. .

podcast.body: Not described beyond being the subject of Death Grips' remixes.

The style established in *Biophilia* was one that Björk was perceived to be moving away from in the lead-up to *Utopia*, as she explored new or revisited old musical avenues. "Veíamos que Bjorky estaba abandonando ese camino en el que se había metido un poco en los últimos discos, en el biofile y el búlmicura."

podcast.body: This album belongs to a later stage in Björk's career where she is viewed more as a museum artist than solely a singer. Her work during this period, alongside *Vulnicura*, delves deeper into audiovisual projects, computer-based creations, and collaborations with other visual artists, solidifying her recognition in the art world. "Esta etapa yo creo que es la que más reconocimiento dentro del mundo del arte ladado al artista Bjork."

This album is identified as the beginning of Björk's extremely pure artistic phase, characterized by a deliberate reduction in production work. It represents a significant shift towards a more natural and organic sound compared to her earlier albums. "el biofilia yo creo que ya empiece a saber etapa de viores que es extremadamente pure, y que prácticamente no tiene trabajo de producción."
